column1: # TIER-2 HELD-OUT CASES, SET 3. Opened 2026-10-30 with TWO rows, both `mechanism: drift`.
# This file exists because sets 1 and 2 are both spent and neither contains a row that
# DEMONSTRATES drift: of the three rows in the whole corpus carrying `mechanism: drift`,
# none meets the strict bar set on 2026-10-30, and two of them are one inferred event. The
# tool's premise is temporal decay at primer sites, so until a row here clears that bar
# the premise is untested.
# THE STRICT BAR (docs/journal/2026-10-30-design-grilled.md Q6): the paper must show the
# SAME LINEAGE CHANGING OVER TIME at primer or probe binding sites -- an alignment, a
# substitution table, or named substitutions with collection years. "Newer isolates fail"
# without that is `coverage`, or not a row at all.
# SCORED 2026-10-30, SO THIS SET IS SPENT. One row agrees and one is undecided:
# INFLUENZA_A_M1_Ward_2004 reads `declining` as of 2013-09-06 (86.2% of 5,847 recent
# records, upper bound below the 90% threshold), which AGREES with Yang 2014 -- the first
# documented failure this project has ever caught by the drift flag itself rather than by
# `low coverage`. On the same records the documented redesign reads `stable` at 91.6%, and
# the two entries differ in nothing but their oligos, which is the control that makes the
# row worth trusting. INFLUENZA_A_HA_H3_CDC_Shu_2026 reads `no recent data`: its archive
# stops in 2018, because the seven H3Nx subtype taxids return 0 records for 2024-2026
# against 95,155 without that restriction. Full record, including the same defect found
# live on the Tsukamoto H5 and H7 entries, in docs/journal/2026-10-30-set3-scored.md.
# IT WAS OPENED AS THE FIRST GENUINE TEST OF THE SCOPED MATRIX, AND IT WAS NOT ONE.
# `scope_taxid` was built on 2026-10-30 and chosen AFTER held-out set 2 had been read, so
# on set 2 it can only be a re-description; these two scopes were read from the source
# papers before any verdict existed, which would have made this a score. NEITHER COULD BE
# HONOURED. The matrix archive's lineage layer sees one lineage: 18 of its 19 metadata
# files predate the `taxid` column and the one that has it reports every record as the
# parent 11320. So a scoped matrix is still untested, and needs a set 4 on an assay whose
# archive resolves below the species. The claim that this file tested it has been corrected
# here rather than left standing.
# THE SECOND ROW LANDED THE SAME DAY. It was written and withheld for part of 2026-10-30,
# because the CDC H3 assay could not be entered: citing the paper that prints its oligos
# rather than the FDA 510(k) that defines it put its design_year 18 years from its DOI's
# year, and papers.citation_matches required them within one. The maintainer's call was to
# teach that check to read a year from the reference text, which citation_problems already
# did -- so CI passed the entry curate refused. Both now share papers.year_agrees,
# measured over every entry with a cached DOI (220) as moving no verdict either way. See
# docs/journal/2026-10-30-citation-year-rule.md.

column5: 10.1128/JCM.02467-13 Yang 2014 J Clin Microbiol 52:76-82: names Ward 2004 as its reference 15 and as "Aw1 in this study" (Discussion), and reports it losing sensitivity to M-gene substitutions that accumulated in the SAME lineage over time -- G238A in 11-12 A(H1N1)pdm09 isolates in 2010-2011, joining C154T (earlier), G225A and T228C through 2012-2013, located by the Fig. 2 alignments in the forward and reverse primer-binding regions. 6 of 40 specimens read negative by Aw1 and positive by the degenerate redesign, and Ct shortened 3.1-14.25 cycles across the H1N1pdm09 panel (Table 1). The redesign is itself in the registry as INFLUENZA_A_M1_Yang_2014. Oligos verified against the held PDF: forward and probe exact, reverse revcomp as printed

column5: 10.1128/jcm.00727-26 Shu 2026 J Clin Microbiol (issued 2026-10-27): the FDA-cleared CDC A(H3) subtyping component losing sensitivity to reverse-primer mismatches that accumulated in one lineage over time -- A21G with T23G/T23C/T23A, the 3C.2a1b.2a clade emerging in 2020 and the mutation reaching 96% of globally circulating viruses by the end of 2021 (GISAID 2020-2023), with a measurable Ct shift between H3 and the H3_v2 redesign and both oligo sets printed in Table 1. 30 of 60 non-subclade-K specimens collected in 2022 carried A21G; 19 of 19 subclade K specimens collected in 2025 carried A21G plus a second mismatch. The redesign is in the registry as INFLUENZA_A_HA_H3_v2_Shu_2026. Both primers verified exact against the held PDF; the probe cannot be machine-verified because Table 1 writes /ZEN/ inside the sequence
